title: GSM Foils Chairman Hired Hitmen to Kill Company's Managing Director Over Rs 32 Crore Debt, Police Say
excerpt: Seven people have been arrested in connection with a murder-for-hire plot targeting the managing director of NSE-listed GSM Foils Limited in Vasai, Maharashtra. The MD survived the shooting and is reported to be stable.
body:
• The chairman of NSE-listed GSM Foils Limited allegedly hired hitmen to kill the company's managing director to avoid repaying Rs 32 crore.
  • Seven people have been arrested in connection with the murder attempt in Vasai, Maharashtra.
  • The managing director survived the firing incident and the company says he is "stable and improving."
  • GSM Foils shares crashed roughly 20% following the incident, despite the company reporting strong first-quarter results.

Police in Maharashtra have arrested seven people in connection with a brazen murder-for-hire plot at NSE-listed SME company GSM Foils Limited, in which the company's chairman allegedly hired hitmen to kill its managing director to avoid repaying a Rs 32 crore debt, according to law enforcement authorities.

The managing director of the Vasai-based aluminium pharma foils manufacturer survived a shooting attack and is reported to be in stable condition. The company issued a statement saying the MD is "stable and improving."

A Corporate Power Struggle Turned Deadly

GSM Foils Limited, which manufactures blister foils and aluminium pharmaceutical packaging, listed on the NSE's SME platform in 2024 after an IPO that was subscribed over 240 times. The company is based in Vasai East, in Mumbai's Palghar district.

According to police, the motive behind the plot was financial. The chairman sought to eliminate the managing director rather than repay Rs 32 crore — approximately $3.8 million — that he owed. Investigators allege that the chairman orchestrated the hiring of contract killers to carry out the attack.

The company's two promoters — the chairman and the MD — together hold more than 73% of the company's shares, according to the most recent shareholding filings. The chairman serves as the company's Chief Financial Officer as well, while the MD has been with the company since its incorporation in June 2023.

Stock Crashes Despite Strong Earnings

The timing of the attack made it all the more jarring for investors. GSM Foils had recently reported strong first-quarter financial results, yet the stock plunged roughly 20% following news of the shooting incident, wiping out significant market value from the micro-cap company.

The dramatic contrast between the company's financial performance and the criminal allegations against its chairman has drawn attention to governance risks in India's rapidly growing SME listing segment, where promoter-driven companies often lack the institutional oversight structures found in larger publicly traded firms.

Seven Arrests, Investigation Ongoing

Police have arrested seven individuals in connection with the plot, including those allegedly hired to carry out the attack. The investigation remains ongoing as authorities work to establish the complete chain of events and determine whether additional individuals were involved in planning the murder attempt.

The case has drawn comparisons to other corporate disputes in India that have escalated to violence, though the involvement of a listed company's top executive as the alleged mastermind is unusual even by those standards.

Implications for India's SME Market

India's SME exchange segment has seen explosive growth in recent years, with hundreds of small companies listing on the NSE and BSE SME platforms. The GSM Foils case highlights vulnerabilities in a segment where corporate governance frameworks are often minimal and power is concentrated among a small group of promoters.

For investors in India's diaspora who have increasingly turned to SME stocks for higher returns, the case serves as a stark reminder that financial due diligence alone may not capture the full spectrum of risks in thinly traded, promoter-dominated companies.

The company has not yet issued a detailed statement regarding the corporate governance implications of the allegations against its chairman.
